summary: Intermittent throughput collapse during nightly batch jobs causing elevated p95 and client 504s on dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on the HelixAI dedicated GPU pool experienced intermittent throughput collapses and request timeouts (504) during the nightly maintenance/batch window. Impact started ~2026-03-10 02:10 UTC and recurred each night for the next two nights until mitigation.

Impact:
- Elevated p95 latency from baseline ~180ms to ~720ms for text generation routes.
- Client-observed 504 errors for streaming and non-streaming requests (~1-3% of requests during peaks).
- HelixAI reported production incidents impacting user-facing features.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: helixai-dpool-usw2 (A100-80GB nodes).
- Autoscaler config: target_gpu_utilization=0.9, cooldown_seconds=300, min_replicas=1, max_replicas=12.
- Scheduled nightly batch jobs (customer-managed) running large batched embedding jobs starting ~02:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Nightly batch job starts and ramps to sustained GPU utilization on one or more nodes.
2) Inference request queue length for HelixAI routes spikes and queue wait times exceed model SLOs.
3) Autoscaler does not scale quickly enough due to cooldown and single-replica minimum; head-of-line requests time out.
4) When autoscaler scales, new nodes join after ~2-5 minutes; performance recovers.

Observed logs/metrics:
- p95 generation latency graph: baseline 150–200ms, spike to 700–800ms for ~3–7 minutes.
- Node-level nvidia-smi sampled at 5s saw sustained 98% GPU utilization and frequent memory allocation spikes during batch window.
- Host CPU at 70–95% during peaks; kubelet logs show scheduling delays.
- Queue length on serving runtime reached 120 requests on affected node shard.
- No system-level OOMs recorded.

Additional notes:
HelixAI runs a combination of short tail inference and large offline embedding batches. Those batches were landing on the same GPU nodes as online inference due to lack of node/pod affinity and insufficient pool isolation.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and hypotheses:
- 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC: Support alerted by HelixAI via email and incident Slack #support-helixai.
- 02:20 UTC: Confirmed elevated p95 and 504s in prod dashboards for helixai-dpool-usw2.
- 02:30 UTC: Correlated spikes with customer-scheduled batch jobs (HelixAI confirmed start times).
- Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor batch processes saturating GPUs and causing head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive inference.
- Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler cooldown and min_replicas settings delay scale-up, amplifying the impact.
- Hypothesis 3: Pod placement allowed batch jobs to co-locate with inference replicas on same CUDA device (no strict anti-affinity).

Data collected:
- Stacktrace/trace-ids from timed-out requests provided by customer (attached in ticket).
- Prometheus timeseries: gpu_utilization, queue_length, pod_startup_time, scheduling_latencies.
- Node logs and nvidia-smi CSV samples pulled for 3 affected nodes.

Partial findings:
- On two nodes, GPUs were at 97–99% utilization for ~4 minutes coinciding with p95 spike.
- Autoscaler observed target exceeded but respected cooldown; first new replica became Ready after ~180s.
- Pod anti-affinity rules were not enforced for HelixAI batch jobs (they used a generic deployment with no dedicated nodeSelector/taints).
- No evidence of kernel-level GPU errors; contention was resource exhaustion rather than driver faults.

Action items raised during investigation:
- Immediate mitigation: advise customer to reschedule or reduce concurrency for nightly batch jobs and provide temporary workaround to pin batch jobs to a separate node pool.
- Infra actions: short-term change to autoscaler cooldown and min_replicas for helixai-dpool-usw2.
- Medium-term: enforce pod anti-affinity / taints+tolerations to isolate batch workloads from latency-sensitive replicas.
- Follow-up ticket to infra team to add per-customer scheduling policies (INT-4421).

resolution:
Workaround applied:
- Migrated HelixAI batch workloads to a new batch-only node pool (customer action with Redwood SRE guidance).
- Temporarily adjusted autoscaler: cooldown_seconds=120, min_replicas=2 for helixai-dpool-usw2.

Permanent / long-term fixes implemented:
- Deployed cluster-level scheduling guardrails to prevent best-effort batch pods from co-locating with latency-sensitive inference replicas (taints + namespace-level tolerations).
- Added per-customer autoscale profiles so critical dedicated pools have conservative min_replicas and faster scale-up. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3342
- Added a runbook entry for customers with mixed workloads recommending batch/job isolation and providing a one-click template to create batch node pools.

Follow-ups:
- INT-4421: infra task to make per-customer scheduling policies configurable via console (assigned to infra team).
- SUP-130010: Outreach to HelixAI to review their job scheduling cadence and to offer managed batch pool setup (CS action).

Incident status: Resolved. Customer confirmed performance back to normal after migration (HelixAI message 2026-03-12 02:18 UTC).
notes:
Key takeaways:
- Mixed workloads (interactive + large batch) on shared dedicated pools can create noisy-neighbor conditions even with GPU-level optimizations.
- Autoscaler tuning must account for scale-up time and VAST batch spikes; conservative min_replicas and shorter cooldowns reduce impact for latency SLOs.
- Provide customers with templates and best-practices for isolating heavy background jobs.
